newsitem.title: USA: Arlen cancels plans to take Starret stake.
newsitem.headline: Arlen cancels plans to take Starret stake.

text.p: Arlen Corp said Friday one of its subsidiaries canceled plans to buy "a substantial interest" in Starret Corp.
Company spokesmen were not immediately available to elaborate on the announcement.
Arlen also said it would file its annual report on form 10-K for the fiscal year ended February 28 with the Securities and Exchange Commission next week.
Starrett, formerly Starrett Housing, is a manufacturer of homes.
The company said on July 16 that it entered into a definitive agreement to merge with entities controlled by Jacob Frydman of real estate investment bank Frydman & Co for $12.25 a share.

"The deal is still on, for $12.25 a share," a Frydman spokesman said in an interview. He added that the original merger agreement included three-parties: Starrett, Frydman's entities and Arlen subsidiary Sub Merger Inc, of which Frydman is president.
"For tax reasons, the Arlen subsidiary dropped out," the spokesman said.
A Starrett spokeswoman was not immediately available for comment. Starrett's stock traded at 11-3/16 Friday late afternoon, down 1/16.
